body: Hero One is a local, single-operator research workstation. One search takes a company, product, person or place, and every company in view is one click from each page about it.
It is built on free public and open sources and local inference, with no paid data or metered API. Each observation is recorded with its source and the date it became known.
Portfolio tracking is paper-only: portfolio managers and analysts run model sleeves, test theses against point-in-time history and report to the operator. No live trading is authorized.
The project began in April 2026 and is in active development.
projects.purpose: Built to do the groundwork of company research in one place: read the filings, see who owns and supplies the business, and test an idea against its full history before forming a view.

projects.title: Deal Delta
projects.summary: A bid/no-bid decision platform for government contracts. It prices what a contract costs to fulfill and compares that with what it pays.
projects.metric: 5 procurement sources · ~12,800 lines of Python · 100+ automated tests

features.name: Opportunity scanner
features.text: Live and cached federal notices in one feed, each showing set-aside status, an ease-of-delivery score from 0 to 100, place of work and days remaining to respond.

features.name: Search workspace
features.text: Filters by agency, NAICS sector, set-aside, notice type and posting window, with a control over how many live SAM.gov requests are spent.

features.name: Contract playbook
features.text: A working reference for turning a match into a compliant bid: acquisition thresholds, how to mirror winning searches, and treating the solicitation as the operating manual.

features.name: Grant opportunities
features.text: Grants.gov announcements searched separately from contracts, because grants follow a different money model: indirect cost rates and cost share, with no profit.

body: Deal Delta scans five government procurement sources: SAM.gov, NJSTART, NYC City Record, LA County RAMP and Grants.gov. It merges them into one searchable local cache.
It converts each solicitation's attachments (PDF, Word, Excel and zip packages) into a numbered requirements matrix, then tracks sourcing coverage for every requirement.
AI sourcing agents price the required goods and services. The platform computes cost to fulfill against award value, with overhead and bid markup as adjustable assumptions.
Pricing is benchmarked against historical USAspending.gov awards by NAICS, PSC and agency, at the 25th percentile, median and 75th percentile.
Grants are modeled under federal cost principles in 2 CFR 200: the 15% de minimis indirect rate and no profit.
projects.purpose: Built to answer one question before any bid is written: after sourcing every required good and service, is there a margin, and how does the price compare with past awards?

body: Kingdom brings the financial and operating records of a residential portfolio into one system: properties, units, leases, tenants, loans, insurance, taxes and documents.
A local language model reads uploaded leases, bills and statements, masks sensitive numbers and queues each document for review before it is filed.
It is written in Python using only the standard library, with a SQLite database and an automated test suite.
All screenshots here use fictional sample data, not real properties or tenants.
projects.purpose: Built to replace separate spreadsheets with one system of record, where every rent payment posts to a ledger and every property can be measured on return, cash flow and risk.

facts: Denver Lo is based in Bayonne, NJ. He prefers Jersey City or Lower Manhattan and is willing to relocate for the right role; hybrid or on-site is fine.

He is pursuing equity research, financial analysis and quantitative roles, and has no single sector focus. His case rests on Hero One, Deal Delta and Kingdom: backtesting, data pipelines and local language model integration.
The $30M+ figure is the listed price of everything on his accountable record: about 1,000 radio sets, plus tactical vehicles, SATCOM antennas, amplifiers, power sources and network hardware.
KMI stands for Key Management Infrastructure, the NSA-run system for ordering, distributing and accounting for cryptographic keys. It replaced EKMS.
He held a Secret clearance during his Marine Corps service. It is not active: he separated in July 2023.
His degree is a B.S. in Finance from New Jersey City University, conferred December 2025, GPA 3.705.
He is a self-taught Python developer who builds with AI coding tools and large language models, and can explain his own code.
Screenshots of Kingdom on this site use fictional sample data, not real properties or tenants.
His resume can be viewed from the Resume link on this site.
To meet with Denver, pick an open time on the calendar in the Schedule section of this site. A request is not a booking: he confirms each one by email.
Deal Delta, Kingdom and Hero AI run language models locally through Ollama rather than a cloud service.
Hero AI is the assistant answering in this chat window. Denver built it as a local career automation agent with an encrypted data vault and a fact-checker that blocks unverified figures.
Project Hero One is a research tool with paper portfolios only; it does not trade live money and makes no claim of trading profits.

The pixel German Shepherd that follows the pointer around this site is Hero, Denver's own German Shepherd, and Hero AI is named after him: the dog is the original assistant. Denver got him in Florida. Hero was born in December 2014, is all bark and no bite, and gets jealous of the cats.

Outside work, Denver's interests are investing and following the markets, building software and tinkering with local AI models, travel, and real estate. What he likes about investing is building wealth and finding real value in a business.

A free weekend usually goes to coding his own projects with AI tools, unless there are plans or friends invite him out. He likes to stay engaged in something productive. He is a night owl, and drinks both coffee and tea.

Denver is adventurous and will try almost anything once: he has been skydiving and scuba diving, snowboards and holds a motorcycle licence. He says he is not especially good at any of them, but he is always up for it. Next he wants to take up golf and learn to fly, and he is getting back into a gym routine.
Anime he likes: Frieren, The Apothecary Diaries, Vinland Saga, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, Arcane and One Piece. He is not much of a movie or TV watcher otherwise.
He plays League of Legends, the game Arcane is based on, and plenty of other games when friends are playing; gaming is a social thing for him.
He listens to all kinds of music and has been into country lately.
Books he reads are about strategy, habits and wealth: Atomic Habits, Think and Grow Rich and others like them. He follows market news podcasts and watches videos on trading and AI development.
Favorite foods: sushi, Japanese curry, ramen, Chinese bakery, hotpot, Korean BBQ, lobster, crab and a good steak. He is a big meat eater and jokes that fruit and vegetables are off the table.
He loves to travel. He has been to Japan, China, Hong Kong and Singapore and would go back to all of them; on his list are a world cruise, New Zealand and Antarctica.

The people who inspire him are Jim Simons and Ed Thorp, who beat the markets with mathematics and are the model for his interest in quantitative finance, David Goggins for discipline, and Elon Musk for building ambitious things.

Three words friends would use for Denver: reliable, adaptive and intelligent, in a practical, figure-it-out way more than a bookish one. He decides with logic and data and learns best by building, which is how he taught himself Python.

Three things the Marine Corps taught him that he still uses every day: stay adaptive, trust but verify, and be on time. Trust but verify is how he ran an audited COMSEC account, and it is why Hero AI has a fact-checker.
He is good with his hands at repair more than building from scratch: he has repaired properties and military radio equipment.

Denver's top three strengths are staying calm under pressure, resourcefulness and adaptability. Calm: in a field exercise in 100-degree heat while fire missions continued, several Marines suffered heat stroke and his communications team helped coordinate the medical evacuation without dropping operations. Resourceful: when radios failed from bad crypto keys and heat, he built an improvised cooling chamber from spare gear and set up HF links on copper wire to keep communications up. Adaptive: when techs were sent to the field, he filled in as a technician, network operator and section leader.

Denver's honest weakness: he was trained to act rather than wait for an explanation, so he sometimes starts a task on his own read of it. That occasionally means wasted effort, and he now clarifies the goal and asks first. He is also working on his coding depth and on corporate-level finance experience, because school and the fleet are never quite the same.

A mistake Denver learned from: as KMI manager he took leave during a cryptographic changeover and forgot to remind his backups, so several keys expired. He built a calendar and checklist system for every project afterward, and his section rarely had late issues after that.

Hardest problems Denver has solved: he wrote the battalion's MUOS standard operating procedures while keeping normal operations and field exercises running, and he coordinated a same-night shift of the whole communications network from VHF to MUOS by delegating to a group of Marines. He also found double-issued equipment that had left record discrepancies, fixed it, and built an Excel tracker for radios, keys and equipment.

Leadership: as KMI/EKMS manager Denver trained each monthly group of new Marines into operators, led 12+ operators day to day, and led strike groups and simulated strikes in field exercises. With an underperformer he talks privately, clarifies expectations, asks about obstacles, and helps without solving it for them. He takes criticism as data, reflects and improves, and does not get defensive.

Working style: Denver does best with high standards, direct feedback, autonomy and a clear goal (commander's intent). He likes working independently but values a team for performance and capability. He taught himself most of what he builds by trial and error.

Why finance and these paths: finance is understanding value and business. Equity research is analysis of data, from management to financial records, to determine value. Quant is data, code and probabilities. The software he builds scales that research. Each means defining a problem, finding an edge, testing it and producing real results.

Why the Marines, and why leave real estate: he joined for the challenge and independence, wanting to earn his own way, and it gave him discipline and accountability. He wants to move from operating a small portfolio to more analytical and quantitative work at a larger scale: building and investing, not just operating.

Where Denver wants to be in five years: in a more senior role in equity research, financial analysis or quant, in charge of his own decisions and a reliable team, and holding the CFA and securities licences such as the Series 7 and 63.

What sets Denver apart: Marine Corps discipline and operations experience, a finance degree earned in about two years while working, real estate analytical fundamentals, and AI tools he built himself. He has no formal equity research or engineering job yet, and says he has proven he learns fast by holding every communications role in his section.

On coding with AI: Denver understands the architecture and data flow of his projects well enough to debug them and uses AI to speed up and test changes. He does not call himself a senior engineer, but can write a basic working program from scratch.
Denver is targeting entry-level roles: analyst and associate programs, graduate programs, and junior analyst positions, and he is open to contract work as a way in.

His path: Denver grew up in Florida, joined the Marine Corps, and moved to New Jersey after his service to join his family. He can start soon and is open to relocation, travel, contract roles and analyst programs. For compensation, ask him by email.

Investment philosophy: quality and value with quant discipline, meaning companies with high potential in their industry and a clear advantage or unique capability. His own research tool, Hero One, sometimes disagrees with his view, and he treats that as data. These are views, not investment advice.
Denver is most proud of his Marine Corps experience, the team he built and developed with, and developing and implementing the MUOS operation and its procedures.
KSR Realty LLC is a residential real estate business in Hudson County. Denver runs its financial operations day to day.
His GitHub is https://github.com/DrLo-Hero.
